evidence.text: Man Wah Holdings (HKEX 1999), a sofa maker that counts DFS among its ten largest European customers, has built a DFS stake with its chairman from 3.17% to 10.18% since 30 Jun. It crossed 10% on 22 Sep, the day Yahoo shows 2.34m shares traded against a ~0.25m median. On 31 Aug the listed company bought 7.68m shares from the chairman's family vehicle at £1.623 a share, about 9% above spot, with a stated aim of a 'closer cooperative relationship'. A price-insensitive strategic buyer that is still active into the print cushions a disappointing guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior results day had a live strategic buyer in the register. On 16 Jul 2026 (H2 order intake -4.4%) the stock fell 5.99% while Man Wah's position sat at about 5%. The next day, 17 Jul, it recovered +7.1% (133.5 to 143.0 on Yahoo daily closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DFS.L?range=4mo&interval=1d), and Man Wah crossed 6% on 29 Jul.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. The English-language record is a string of TR-1 forms with no commentary. I found no English article framing Man Wah as a strategic or possible bidder, and no mention that it paid 162.3p, above today's price. If the market read this as bid interest the stock would carry a premium to the 162p Man Wah paid. Instead it sits at 148.5, below that and below the 165 of late August. The one visible repricing is today's +7% intraday on 1.36m shares after the 09:05 TR-1, and that is why this is sized small: a good part of it is already in the window's opening price.
evidence.independence: The TR-1 series on Investegate and the HKEX connected-transaction filing are separate documents from separate regulators. They show the same buyer, so this counts as one finding. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0831/2026083100921.pdf

evidence.text: Container freight has roughly doubled into FY27, and DFS itself sizes that exposure: 'every $1,000 movement in freight rate per container impacts our annual freight cost charge by c.£7m-£8m a year'. Drewry Shanghai to Rotterdam ran $4,287-4,682 per FEU from July to August 2026 and $3,626 on 17 Sep, against $2,840 in January 2026, and the composite WCI stood at $1,669-1,959 in Oct-Nov 2025. So a $1,000-1,500 sustained gap is £7-12m against a FY27 consensus of £48.0m that assumes +7% PBT growth on +0.9% revenue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Freight turned from tailwind into a headwind within FY25: a -120bp gross-margin hit disclosed in the FY25 prelims (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dfs-furniture--dfs/fy25-preliminary-results/9130219). The stock rose 2.0% that day because the company said it was 'comfortable with consensus'. The last time DFS's outlook disappointed (16 Jul 2026, weaker H2 demand) it fell 5.99%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, so sized small. The sensitivity is in DFS's own FY25 results and the freight index is public, so the sell-side can do this arithmetic. The company-compiled FY27 consensus was refreshed on 16 Sep, after the freight spike, and still shows +7% growth. So either analysts expect mitigation or rates to fall, which is happening: -9% on the week to 17 Sep as Suez reopens. If the market had priced a freight-driven FY27 cut, the FY27 consensus on DFS's own page would sit at or below FY26's £44.8m, not at £48.0m. The residual is a probability-weighted chance the new CFO (Dominique Highfield, on the board since 5 May 2026) guides below that number.
evidence.independence: Drewry WCI via Daily Cargo News, 17 Sep 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-17-september-2026), 2 Jul 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-2-july-2026), 13 Aug 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-13-august-2026) and 8 Jan 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-8-january-2026). evidence.text: The price has de-rated about 41% since the June update (1,051p on 5 Jun to 615p on 23 Sep, low 519p on 15 Sep), but the company's own consensus page, updated 1 Sep, still shows FY26 adjusted EBITDA at $57.8m and FY27 at $56.8m. So a plain FY reaffirmation would land against a price that already embeds an estimate cut the sell-side has not made.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-line surprises on this stock: 5 Jun 2026 FY upgrade +27.63%; 31 Mar 2026 FY25 beat with FY26 'in line' +47.09%; 13 Jan 2026 year-end update with DRAM uncertainty -2.14% close to close (about -7.5% intraday per Alliance News); 29 Jan 2025 trading update -3.85%. evidence.why_not_priced: If the market believed $57.8m FY26 and flat FY27, the shares would not sit 41% below the level they reached on the upgrade that produced those numbers. The price is discounting a cut (Berenberg says the low-cost memory is 'almost depleted') that the published consensus has not taken. What is not priced is the chance that the company confirms the number. The evidence for that chance is the absence of any warning RNS between the 1 Sep consensus refresh and the print, which MAR would require if FY were materially below the figure on its own website. That is inference from silence, so the size is small and the band is wide.
evidence.independence: Uses a different document from finding 2. evidence.text: In a Reg FD 8-K furnished 2026-07-08, GitLab restated the Duo Agent Platform paid Consumption Run Rate it had touted five weeks earlier as 'nearly $20 million' down to approximately $15 million, because the calculation 'now excludes certain one-time credit incentives granted to paying customers' - i.e. roughly a quarter of the headline AI number the street heard in June was credits given away to existing paying seats, not incremental purchase.
evidence.why_not_priced: The restatement was buried in a furnished (not filed) Item 7.01 8-K whose only exhibit is a 48-slide deck rendered as 48 JPEG images (exhibit991-businessupdat001.jpg through 048.jpg), so it is not machine-readable and not searchable; every write-up of that filing led on the forward number instead, e.g. Quiver headlined it 'GitLab Jumps as Investor Update Highlights Faster Consumption Growth and AI Product Traction'. If the market had priced the giveaway component, the sell-side previews into this print would be arguing about credit gross margin rather than 'Duo traction', and the stock would not be trading at $45.64 against a 28-broker consensus target of $38.92 with three brokers only just chasing it up from $35-36 in the last week of August.
evidence.independence: Independent corroboration of the giveaway mechanic and its cost, from a different document: the Q1 FY27 call, where CEO William Staples described 'promotional credits that we've given in this first quarter of availability' letting developers 'experiment with Duo Agent platform before the organization needs to commit', and the Q1 release shows non-GAAP gross margin of 88% versus 90% a year earlier while CFO Jessica Ross attributed the 88% to favourable SaaS mix rather than inference cost - https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/03/gitlab-gtlb-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ and https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260602438182/en/GitLab-Reports-First-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2027-Financial-Results . NOTE: shares the 2026-07-08 8-K as a source with finding 2 below, which reads the same document in the opposite direction.

evidence.text: GitLab's FY27 guidance explicitly embeds no material Duo Agent Platform revenue contribution, yet the company went out of its way one month into Q2 to confirm paid CRR had gone from ~$15M at 30 April to above $20M at 30 June on the same restated basis - a ~33% step-up in two months on a line that is upside-only versus the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: A voluntary mid-quarter Reg FD business update is a management-confidence tell that aggregators record as a press-release row and nothing more; GTLB did not sustain a re-rating in July, and the +28.26% 20-day run-up in the baseline dates from the 26-27 August sector-wide AI-software melt-up, not from GitLab-specific consumption news. The clearest evidence it is unpriced is that the consensus Q2 revenue estimate (~$273.1-273.3M) sits inside the company's own $272-274M guide, i.e. the street is modelling a zero beat on a company whose Q1 revenue came in about four points above its guided growth rate - if the consumption upside were priced, estimates would sit above the guide, not on it.
evidence.independence: The mid-quarter CRR trajectory itself comes from the 2026-07-08 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1653482/000165348226000145/gtlb-20260708.htm), which is the SAME document finding 1 rests on - flagging that explicitly; the independent leg here is the Q1 transcript, a different document, in which the CFO lists 'no material DAP revenue contribution in FY27' as one of four prudence items baked into the raised full-year guide.

If it were priced, the stock would not be -16.75% over twenty sessions into a print that can mechanically deliver ~7% of market cap in cash, and previews would frame the quarter around a tariff recovery instead of quoting a garbled adjusted-EPS consensus that aggregators variously print as $0.25, $0.22 and -$0.06. The claim-sale-to-an-Investor structure is also unique to DBI among footwear names and is not something a screen surfaces.
evidence.independence: Caleres, a footwear importer whose Q2 ended 2 Aug 2026 (one day after DBI's 1 Aug quarter end), reported on 2026-09-09 that it recognised $55.6m of IEEPA tariff recoveries in cost of goods sold, which establishes that CBP CAPE payouts to footwear importers actually landed inside this exact fiscal window rather than slipping to Q3: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CAL/caleres-reports-second-quarter-2026-cbjhhvcqm4mz.html . evidence.text: DBI's FY26 guidance conservatism rests on an assumption management stated on 9 Jun 2026 — that 'a substantial portion of any potential refunds will be offset by increased risk from the new Section 301 tariffs that may begin in August' — but the August step-up replaced an expiring Section 122 10% surcharge (lapsed 24 Jul 2026) with a two-tier 10%/12.5% Section 301 forced-labour duty, an incremental 0-2.5pp rather than a new layer, and Caleres guided H2 gross margin up 150-200bp citing 'lower current tariff rates'.
